forces.title: Agentic AI transforms business processes, reducing coordination costs
forces.description: The advent of agentic AI is fundamentally altering how business processes are managed. By automating verification, reconciliation, and routing at workflow interfaces, AI can significantly reduce human-mediated handoffs and associated "coordination tax." This shifts BPO from task automation to managing AI-driven continuous flows, requiring new skillsets focused on exception handling and strategic oversight, moving beyond traditional manual process execution.
forces.source_title: Cutting the ‘coordination tax’: How agentic AI can reshape workflows

forces.title: AI adoption transforming healthcare BPO and clinical trial operations
forces.description: The increasing adoption of AI and machine learning in clinical trials, including by CROs, represents a significant structural shift for healthcare BPO. While many companies are piloting AI tools, the greatest performance gains are reported by those that redesign roles and workflows around AI. This will likely push healthcare BPO providers to integrate AI into their service offerings, moving towards more data-driven and automated trial operations, influencing how services like patient recruitment and trial monitoring are delivered.
forces.source_title: Clinical Trials Face Persistent Challenges—and New Opportunities

forces.title: Food & Beverage sector re-insourcing due to automation
forces.description: Food and beverage producers in Ireland are increasingly investing in automation and robotics to boost productivity, manage costs, and address labor shortages. A notable trend is "bringing selected outsourced activities in-house" and upskilling employees to manage automated environments. This shift towards internalizing previously outsourced functions presents a headwind for BPO providers targeting this sector, as clients reduce reliance on external services for certain operational activities.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Shift from task automation to AI-driven workflow redesign
forces.description: The industry is undergoing a structural shift where AI's true economic value is realized not by automating isolated tasks, but by redesigning end-to-end workflows. This implies that BPO providers must evolve from offering basic task outsourcing to providing advanced services that incorporate AI for strategic decision-making, process optimization, and enhanced operational outcomes for clients. Failure to adapt to this model risks being bypassed by competitors offering more integrated, AI-centric solutions.
forces.source_title: The decision dividend: How AI creates economic value

forces.title: AI-driven commercial transformation enhances BPO value proposition
forces.description: For BPO providers, AI-led commercial transformation presents a significant upside. AI applications in pricing optimization (2-5% revenue uplift), lead generation (5-15% revenue uplift), and sales productivity (reducing non-sales activities from 40% to 15%) can be integrated into BPO offerings. This allows BPO firms to deliver superior outcomes for clients by leveraging AI to improve margin discipline, systematize new client acquisition, and enhance frontline execution, shifting BPO services towards higher-value, data-driven commercial processes.
forces.source_title: How AI-led commercial transformation can power industrial growth

forces.title: AI redefines category management, impacting KPO service models
forces.description: AI is fundamentally redefining category management in distribution, moving beyond human-led processes to agent-led with human-in-the-loop and fully agentic models. This structural shift requires distributors to invest in upskilling and establish clear human-agent teaming and decision rights. For BPO providers offering KPO (knowledge process outsourcing) services, this means adapting their offerings to integrate AI, focusing on providing expertise in AI governance, data literacy, analytical judgment, and supporting the transition to AI-driven insights rather than just traditional category management tasks.
forces.source_title: How AI is redefining category management in distribution

forces.title: Hospitality sector adopts AI/automation for back-office and CXM
forces.description: The Irish hospitality sector is increasingly focusing on operational efficiency through AI and automation, particularly for back-office processes like rostering, revenue management, guest communications (CXM), and energy monitoring. This trend is driven by the need to reduce operational friction, optimize costs, and reframe labor strategy towards a smaller, more skilled workforce. For BPO providers, this represents an opportunity to offer technology-led services that automate repetitive tasks and enable redeployment of client staff to high-value guest-facing roles.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: AI-enabled pricing optimization boosts BPO value for distributors
forces.description: Advances in AI, particularly Gen AI, are revolutionizing pricing strategies for distributors by enabling automated product data enrichment, dynamic self-learning pricing engines, and systematic margin protection through contract intelligence. A building materials distributor, for example, achieved a sixfold speed improvement in product data processing and over 200 basis points margin expansion. BPO providers can leverage these capabilities to offer high-value services in pricing architecture, contract management, and sales support, enhancing their strategic role beyond traditional process execution.
forces.source_title: Pricing in distribution: A strategic growth engine

forces.title: Organizational rewiring for AI becomes critical for BPO competitiveness
forces.description: The shift from merely deploying AI tools to fundamentally redesigning operating models and workflows is a critical structural change. McKinsey emphasizes that this "organizational rewiring" drives the most significant EBIT impact, enabling AI systems to synthesize information, make decisions, and coordinate workflows across teams. For BPO providers, this means that competitive advantage will increasingly depend on their ability to lead and implement such deep organizational transformations for clients, offering services that go beyond process automation to include strategic consulting on AI-enabled operating models and talent redeployment.
forces.source_title: The operating model advantage: Why AI winners are rewiring their organizations

forces.title: AI's automation potential (60% of work hours) reshaping BPO scope
forces.description: McKinsey estimates that close to 60% of work hours are theoretically automatable by AI agents and intelligent robots, giving rise to a "symbiotic enterprise" model. This structural change implies a radical shift for BPO services, moving from managing large human workforces to orchestrating AI agents and handling exceptions. Traditional BPO advantages, such as workforce scale and manual process efficiency, will erode, forcing providers to reinvent their execution models and develop new capabilities in AI governance and integration to remain competitive.

forces.title: Risk of customer re-insourcing and AI-native BPO competition
forces.description: The emergence of the "symbiotic enterprise" model, driven by advanced AI capabilities, poses a key risk to traditional BPO providers. With AI eroding advantages related to workforce scale and coordination complexity, clients may find it easier to re-insource processes. Furthermore, new AI-native competitors, unburdened by legacy operating models, could challenge incumbents. BPO firms face the imperative to transform their offerings strategically or risk losing market share to these evolving competitive dynamics.

forces.title: Managing "cognitive tax" and overreach in AI deployments
forces.description: As enterprises become strategically dependent on AI providers and deploy autonomous systems, McKinsey identifies new risks: a "cognitive tax" on execution and the danger of overreach. BPO providers, as partners in AI implementation, must carefully manage the complexities of technology integration, vendor relationships, and ensuring that AI deployments align with organizational absorption and governance capabilities. Failure to do so could lead to costly errors, operational disruptions, or an inability to realize projected benefits, impacting service delivery.

forces.title: AI reducing demand for some services and staffing needs
forces.description: In Norway, some businesses report that digital solutions and the emergence of artificial intelligence are reducing their need for employees and certain services. This trend, noted by Norges Bank's Regional Network, suggests a potential contraction in demand for traditional BPO services that rely on human labor for routine tasks. For BPO providers, this necessitates a shift towards AI-integrated or higher-value services to remain relevant as clients internalize or automate previous outsourced functions.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

forces.title: Digital and AI leverage essential for supply chain operations
forces.description: Irish manufacturing firms recognize supply chain visibility, resilience, and agility as strategic imperatives, driven by multiple shocks (Brexit, Covid19, Ukraine, Middle East conflict). To achieve this, companies are focusing on building and resourcing operations teams by leveraging digital and AI technologies to anchor supply chain decisions in data. This creates a tailwind for BPO providers that can offer advanced, AI-powered supply chain management and KPO services to support these strategic initiatives for manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI drives workflow redesign, unlocking significant operating leverage
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that agentic AI is transforming enterprise operations by automating coordination at workflow interfaces, reducing “coordination tax” (costs of human handoffs). This enables redesign of end-to-end processes, not just individual tasks. Examples show tenfold improvements in planning speed and 80% touchless operations, resulting in billions in profit impact for industrial manufacturers within two years. The firm notes that while AI improves individual productivity, the true value lies in organizational rewiring, shifting human roles to higher-value decision-making and exception management rather than headcount reduction.
viewpoints.source_title: Cutting the ‘coordination tax’: How agentic AI can reshape workflows

viewpoints.title: AI reshaping clinical trial workflows, delivering significant performance gains
viewpoints.description: Bain's survey on clinical trials indicates widespread AI experimentation, with 65% of sponsors and Contract Research Organizations (CROs) piloting AI tools. Crucially, 16% of these organizations are moving beyond mere tool adoption by actively reshaping roles and workflows around AI capabilities. This deeper integration is reported to power the greatest performance gains, underscoring that organizational redesign, not just technology deployment, is key to realizing AI's full potential in healthcare BPO contexts.
viewpoints.source_title: Clinical Trials Face Persistent Challenges—and New Opportunities

viewpoints.title: AI's economic value stems from workflow redesign, not just tool deployment
viewpoints.description: McKinsey argues that most organizations fail to realize measurable earnings impact from AI because they simply layer copilots and chatbots onto existing processes. Companies that fundamentally redesign end-to-end workflows around AI, however, achieve significant economic benefits, including a roughly 20% EBITDA uplift and one-to-two-year payback periods. This approach prioritizes workflow transformation before technology selection, driving value through faster decisions, better asset utilization, and improved opportunity capture, rather than solely labor cost reduction.
viewpoints.source_title: The decision dividend: How AI creates economic value

viewpoints.title: AI success requires operating model redesign, not just technology deployment
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that despite widespread AI adoption, few companies achieve meaningful enterprise-wide impact because they "bolt-on" AI to existing structures. Only 21% of companies fundamentally redesign their operating models around AI. Top performers, however, who attribute 5% or more of EBIT to AI, are three times more likely to pursue broad operating model redesign and twice as likely to redesign workflows before selecting AI tools. This approach, focused on rewiring organizations and eliminating coordination complexity, is key to capturing AI's full economic potential.
viewpoints.source_title: The operating model advantage: Why AI winners are rewiring their organizations

viewpoints.title: Symbiotic enterprise redefines work, AI automating 60% of hours
viewpoints.description: McKinsey foresees the rise of the "symbiotic enterprise," where AI agents and intelligent robots become a significant part of the workforce, potentially automating close to 60% of work hours. The firm emphasizes that meaningful P&L impact comes from reinventing execution and redesigning workflows around hybrid human–AI collaboration, rather than merely augmenting existing processes. This new model will erode traditional advantages like workforce scale and coordination complexity, necessitating a strategic transformation for businesses, including BPO providers, to avoid incrementalism or overreach.

demand_drivers.description: Organizations seek to reduce hidden coordination costs (35-60% of work time) and latency in workflows through AI automation.
AI enables compression of decision cycles from weeks to days or hours, improving responsiveness to market changes and operational issues.

pnl_drivers.description: Same people produce more revenue through AI-driven efficiency, leading to operating leverage without direct headcount cuts.
Better and faster decisions enabled by AI optimize production schedules and maintenance plans, increasing output from existing assets.

new_opportunities.description: AI allows for fundamental rethinking of processes, moving beyond task automation to eliminate coordination friction between steps.
Employees are redeployed from routine coordination tasks to higher-value roles focusing on strategic decisions, exceptions, and AI system management.

Increasing policy prioritization of independent living and care closer to home (e.g., home support hours) boosts demand for distributed healthcare services.
Persistent operational challenges from staffing issues, funding adequacy, and rising costs pressure provider margins, potentially increasing interest in BPO solutions to manage these overheads.

demand_drivers.description: Retailers and wholesalers face increased overheads from minimum wage increments, pension auto-enrolment, insurance, energy, and global commodity prices, driving demand for cost-efficient BPO solutions.

A 'full employment' environment makes recruitment and retention of personnel a key challenge, pushing businesses to seek external BPO support for HR or other functions to manage staffing gaps and reduce burden.
Intense competition and cost increases compel businesses to prioritize margin development, making BPO attractive for streamlining non-core operations and improving efficiency.

new_opportunities.description: BPO providers can offer services to help Irish retail convenience businesses manage rising operational costs and mitigate recruitment/retention challenges through outsourcing non-core functions or specialized HR BPO.

The sector has experienced a sustained squeeze in margins over the past three years, increasing the impetus for cost optimization through efficient process management, potentially via BPO.
